slides.title: You write a to-do list.
slides.text: Everything you keep is {data}. Your list keeps changing; the photo of the leaking tap you attach never will. Both are data.
slides.deep: The list is a Doc (story 3): CRDT maps, lists and text. The photo is a Value: immutable bytes named by their BLAKE3 hash, streamed in verified chunks.

slides.title: The list starts from itself.
slides.text: When data is born, it gets a {seal}: a key used exactly once, to sign the data's first {rule}, a signed statement of who may do what, naming its owner, and then destroyed. Nobody holds the seal, so nobody can share it, lose it or steal it. The list doesn't come from any account; its authority starts with itself.
slides.deep: The seal is a fresh Ed25519 key pair. Its public key is the data ID. It signs one certificate, naming the owner, and the private key is zeroised. Keyhive calls the same pattern the genesis key.

slides.title: Its first rule makes you the owner.
slides.text: The seal's one signature names a single {owner}: you. The owner may do everything, for good, including writing the rules for everyone else. There is always exactly one owner: an identity, never a group.
slides.deep: The owner is an identity ID inside the first certificate. Its authority never expires and only the owner can sign a hand-over. Ownership is never a set, so there is no removing someone from it. (D5, D30)

slides.title: Data comes in two kinds.
slides.text: A {Doc} is data that changes: a list, a note, a calendar. A {Value} is bytes that never change: a photo, a PDF, a movie. Together they cover everything.
list: Doc: any JSON that changes, built from CRDT data types that merge by themselves.
Value: any file that never changes, named by its hash.
slides.deep: Doc: a Loro document, a history of CRDT ops. Value: immutable bytes addressed by BLAKE3, fetched in verified ranges (iroh-blobs style).

slides.title: A Doc looks like JSON.
slides.text: Under the hood it's built from {CRDT} data types: maps, lists, text, trees and counters. CRDT means: copies can be changed separately and always merge back into the same result. Your to-do list is a map holding a title and a list of items.
slides.deep: CRDT containers: map, list, movable list, text, tree, counter. The JSON you see is a projection of their current state.

slides.title: A Value never changes.
slides.text: Its name is the hash of its bytes, so it can't be swapped without everyone noticing. It travels in ranges, and you fetch only the parts you need: the first minute of a movie, page 3 of a PDF.
slides.deep: BLAKE3 builds a hash tree over 1 KiB blocks, so any range can be verified against the root hash alone. Change one byte and the name changes.

slides.title: Every Value has its own Doc.
slides.text: The movie never changes, but its name, its notes and who may see it do. So every Value comes with a small Doc: its metadata. The Doc also holds the Value's key, so whoever may read the Doc can open the Value.

code.name: Leaking tap
code.value_key: sealed with this Doc's data key

slides.deep: A Value's data key is stored inside its metadata Doc, under that Doc's own data key. Read on the Doc implies read on the Value. Taking read away protects only future versions of an immutable Value.

slides.title: Data, in short.
list: Everything you keep is data, and every piece of data starts from itself.
Its seal names exactly one owner, an identity.
A Doc is JSON that changes; a Value is bytes that never change.
Every Value has a Doc for its metadata and its key.
slides.deep: Data IDs are seal public keys; Value names are BLAKE3 hashes; Docs are CRDT documents.
